answer: Trust propagates from anchored attestations through bounded random walks on the graph, so a sybil set \(S\) receives voting weight only through walks that reach it. If \(S\) has low conductance—few crossing edges relative to its volume—the per-step escape probability is small, and over \(L\) steps is at most \(L\phi(S)\) under stationary conditioning. Thus, for fixed seed mass and capped walks, its aggregate weight is bounded; “wharf” and “quill” are merely vertex labels, not independent trust.
